## Overview

Flavescence dorée is a quarantine disease of grapevine, caused by a phytoplasma
carried from vine to vine by the leafhopper *Scaphoideus titanus*. Infected vines
show symptoms the year after infection and are uprooted (rogued) the following
winter. @Adrakey2023 mapped every vine of three plots at Faleyras, near
Bordeaux, in 2018 and 2019, and fitted a yearly spatial epidemic model by Markov
chain Monte Carlo with data augmentation, comparing dispersal kernels and ways
of modelling infection from outside the plots. This vignette fits the zoo's
`flavescence_doree`, an adaptation of their model, to the same maps with
CellularAutomataInference.

The main difference from the source is primary infection. The source's best
model scales infection from outside the plots by the number of symptomatic
vines within 300 m the year before, counted by a regional surveillance
programme whose data were not released; here it is a constant rate.

```{julia}
#| output: false
ENV["GKSwstype"] = "100"
using EcologicalCellularAutomata
using CellularAutomataCore
using CellularAutomataInference
using Distributions
using Plots
using Random
using Statistics
```

## The maps

```{julia}
#| label: fig-maps
#| fig-cap: "The three plots (left, the Cabernet Sauvignon plot CS; right, the Merlot plots M1 and M2): vines symptomatic in 2018 (red) and 2019 (orange), absent by 2018 or 2019 (grey), and healthy (light green)."
v = fd_vines()
colours = Dict(:symptomatic_2018 => :red, :symptomatic_2019 => :orange,
               :absent_2018 => :gray40, :absent_2019 => :gray70, :healthy => :lightgreen)
scatter(v.x, v.y; color=[colours[s] for s in v.status], markersize=1.2,
        markerstrokewidth=0, aspect_ratio=1, legend=false, xlabel="east (m)",

```

```{julia}
for s in (:absent_2018, :symptomatic_2018, :absent_2019, :symptomatic_2019, :healthy)
    println(rpad(s, 18), count(==(s), v.status))
end
```

## The model and its likelihood

Each yearly step is a season. A healthy vine is removed for other reasons with
probability $q$; otherwise it is infected with probability
$1 - \exp\{-(\varepsilon + \beta \sum_j c_j K(r_{ij}; \alpha)/\alpha^2)\}$,
summing over the vines symptomatic that season, within a cut-off radius. An
infected vine is symptomatic the next season, infecting others, and is rogued
the winter after. The survey fixes almost every vine's history: a vine
symptomatic in 2018 or 2019 was infected two seasons before; a Merlot vine
absent in 2019 was removed for another reason; the Cabernet Sauvignon plot was
uprooted after the 2018 survey; and a vine healthy in 2019 may or may not have
been infected in 2018, which is summed over. Only the 411 vines absent in 2018
are unknown: each was either rogued after showing symptoms in 2015, 2016 or
2017, or removed for another reason in some year before 2018.
`fd_survey_fit` builds these histories, `fd_loglik` gives their exact
probability (equal to the core's `path_logpdf` on complete histories, as the
package's tests check), and `fd_latent_step!` updates the unknown ones.

## Fitting

The priors follow the source's code: exponential, with means 0.012 for
$\varepsilon$, 10 for $\beta$ and 100 m for $\alpha$, and uniform for $q$.
Four chains of the power-law kernel $(1 + r/\alpha)^{-6}$ (the source's
preferred shape) with a cut-off of 120 m:

```{julia}
priors = (ε=Exponential(0.012), β=Exponential(10), q=Uniform(0, 1), α=Exponential(100))
θ0 = (ε=0.005, β=20.0, q=0.003, α=30.0)
function fit_kernel(kernel, radius, iterations)
    prob = problem_flavescence_doree(; kernel, radius)
    fit, z0 = fd_survey_fit(prob)
    model = AugmentedModel((θ, z) -> fd_loglik(θ, z, fit),
                           (rng, z, θ) -> fd_latent_step!(rng, z, θ, fit), priors, z0)
    chains = sample(Xoshiro(4), model, DataAugmentation(; parameter_steps=3, init_scale=0.05),
                    MCMCThreads(), iterations, 4; progress=false, initial_params=fill(θ0, 4),
                    discard_initial=2_000)
    return (; prob, fit, chains, summary=posterior_summary(chains))
end
main = fit_kernel(:power6, 120.0, 6_000)
r3(x) = round(x; sigdigits=3)
for k in keys(main.summary)
    q = main.summary[k].q
    println(rpad(k, 3), r3(q[2]), " [", r3(q[1]), ", ", r3(q[3]), "]  R-hat ",
            round(main.summary[k].rhat; digits=3), "  ESS ", round(Int, main.summary[k].ess))
end
```

The removal rate $q$, about 0.003 a year, is close to the source's 0.004-0.005.
The kernel's scale is not: $\alpha$ is about 120 m, so within the plots the
kernel barely falls, and infection spreads on the scale of the plots, where the
source found a mean distance of 13 m to the first infection.

## Kernels

```{julia}
alts = [(:exponential, fit_kernel(:exponential, 60.0, 4_000)),
        (:gaussian, fit_kernel(:gaussian, 60.0, 4_000))]
for (name, f) in alts
    s = f.summary
    println(rpad(name, 12), "α ", r3(s.α.q[2]), " m [", r3(s.α.q[1]), ", ", r3(s.α.q[3]),
            "], ε ", r3(s.ε.q[2]), ", β ", r3(s.β.q[2]), ", q ", r3(s.q.q[2]))
end
```

Every shape is broad. With the source's regional term absent, infections far from
the 2018 sources (the far side of the Merlot plots) can only come from a long
kernel or a high background rate, and the fit uses both.

## Does the fit reproduce the maps?

Simulations from 100 draws of the main fit's posterior, from 2013, compared with
the survey: the number of vines symptomatic in each plot in 2018 and 2019, and
how far each vine newly symptomatic in 2019 lies from the nearest vine
symptomatic in 2018.

```{julia}
draws = reduce(vcat, [c.values for c in main.chains])
idx = round.(Int, range(1, size(draws, 1); length=100))
plots = ["CS", "M1", "M2"]
obs_counts = [count(i -> v.plot[i] == pl && v.status[i] === s, eachindex(v.x))
              for pl in plots, s in (:symptomatic_2018, :symptomatic_2019)]
xy = hcat(v.x, v.y)
function nearest_distance(new, old)
    isempty(old) && return NaN
    return median(minimum(hypot(xy[i, 1] - xy[j, 1], xy[i, 2] - xy[j, 2]) for j in old)
                  for i in new)
end
obs_near = nearest_distance(findall(==(:symptomatic_2019), v.status),
                            findall(==(:symptomatic_2018), v.status))
sim_counts = zeros(Int, 3, 2, length(idx))
sim_near = Float64[]
for (k, i) in enumerate(idx)
    θ = (ε=draws[i, 1], β=draws[i, 2], q=draws[i, 3], α=draws[i, 4])
    pr = problem_flavescence_doree(; kernel=:power6, radius=120.0, α=θ.α,
                                   seed=500 + k, pmap=(ε=θ.ε, β=θ.β, q=θ.q))
    sol = solve(pr; saveat=[5, 6], save_start=false)
    s18 = fd_symptomatic(sol.u[1], pr.p.cells)
    s19 = fd_symptomatic(sol.u[2], pr.p.cells) .& (v.plot .!= "CS")
    for (a, pl) in enumerate(plots)
        sim_counts[a, 1, k] = count(s18 .& (v.plot .== pl))
        sim_counts[a, 2, k] = count(s19 .& (v.plot .== pl))
    end
    push!(sim_near, nearest_distance(findall(s19), findall(s18)))
end
println("plot  year  survey  simulated median [90%]")
for (a, pl) in enumerate(plots), (b, y) in enumerate((2018, 2019))
    sims = sim_counts[a, b, :]
    println(rpad(pl, 6), y, lpad(obs_counts[a, b], 8), "   ", median(sims), " [",
            quantile(sims, 0.05), ", ", quantile(sims, 0.95), "]")
end
println("median distance from a 2019 case to the nearest 2018 case: survey ",
        round(obs_near; digits=1), " m, simulated ",
        round(median(filter(isfinite, sim_near)); digits=1), " m [",
        round(quantile(filter(isfinite, sim_near), 0.05); digits=1), ", ",
        round(quantile(filter(isfinite, sim_near), 0.95); digits=1), "]")
```

The fit does not reproduce the maps. Simulated from 2013 with every vine
equally susceptible and a constant background rate, the epidemic spreads evenly:
far too few vines are symptomatic in the Cabernet Sauvignon plot in 2018 (the
survey found 665, 29% of the plot), too many in M2, too few in M1 in 2019, and
new cases lie closer to old ones than in the survey. The data augmentation fits
the histories given the maps, but the model cannot generate a plot as heavily
infected as CS next to plots as lightly infected as the Merlot ones. Differences
in susceptibility or exposure between plots and cultivars (the source includes
a cultivar effect on infectivity, and found most of the 2019 Merlot cases near
the infected CS plot), the epidemic's start in CS, and the regional primary
infection are what is missing.

## Summary

| Question | Answer here |
|:---|:---|
| Removal for other reasons | about 0.003 a year, close to the source's 0.004-0.005 |
| The dispersal kernel | broad for every shape (scale near 120 m for the power law), where the source found 13 m |
| Why the difference | primary infection is constant here; the source's best model scales it by regional counts that were not released, which absorbs the distant infections |
| Counts and spatial pattern | not reproduced: too few cases in the Cabernet Sauvignon plot in 2018, too many in M2, and new cases too close to old ones |
